claim: For Component Intelligence v0.1, the choice that matters most is not graph versus typed records versus rules. It is whether every engineering value carries its own epistemic state (KNOWN, UNKNOWN or ASSUMED) and its own provenance, and whether that survives every stage boundary through to CAD. OMNI's current downstream layers cannot carry UNKNOWN or source class, and they quietly replace a missing value with a concrete one. The CAD IR gives every dimension a numeric default. Unregistered component types become a 50x30x15 mm box. Deserialization silently drops fields it doesn't recognize. OMNI has at least four status vocabularies that don't match, and only one includes UNKNOWN, which no code in mission_graph reads. Reliability scoring averages BLOCKED gates into a single confidence number. Provenance marks every agent's output 'llm_generated' and has no classes like STANDARD or MANUFACTURER. So a Component Intelligence layer could correctly produce UNKNOWN or FAIL findings (for example 'bearing speed rating unavailable' or 'bore does not match seat') and still lose them when it plugs into the existing pipeline: they would become plausible geometry and a positive score. Prediction: unless v0.1 makes (a) a value-level Known/Unknown type with provenance and (b) typed CAD obligations the only path into CAD, with a boundary check that rejects defaulted values, the architecture will not fail closed in practice, however good its rule engine is. The CAD layer currently has no mechanical assembly concepts at all, so v0.1 can define this boundary from scratch rather than retrofit it.
mechanism:
The mission requires that UNKNOWN is never silently turned into PASS. In this repository, missing information is lost at the stage boundaries rather than inside a rule evaluator. There are four ways it happens.

(1) Geometry defaults. MechanicalComponentSpec uses length_mm=0.0 to mean 'use library default'. `_component()` in cad_detail_pass_planner always fills it from `default_dims()`, which returns (50.0, 30.0, 15.0) for any unregistered type. `component_shape()` falls back to 'box'. MountingFeatureSpec and FastenerPatternSpec default to diameter_mm 6.0 and 3.2. A bearing whose bore is unknown, handed to this IR, would therefore become concrete placeholder geometry with no finding.

(2) Schema filtering. `AssemblySpec.from_dict` keeps only keys in `__dataclass_fields__`. Any upstream `status`, `provenance` or `unknown` annotation not already in the dataclass is silently discarded.

(3) Status collapse. The vocabularies are:
- reliability: PASS/WARN/FAIL/BLOCKED, with no UNKNOWN
- mission_graph ValidationCheck: PASS/WARNING/FAIL/UNKNOWN, but UNKNOWN has no reader in mission_graph
- engineering validation_engine: lowercase pass/warning/blocked
- findings_projection: severities only, where an empty severity becomes 'warning' and status is always 'open'

`compute_engineering_confidence` averages BLOCKED at 0.1 alongside PASS at 1.0, so enough passing gates can outweigh an unknown in the single confidence number.

(4) Provenance flattening. ProvenanceRef.evidence_type defaults to 'llm_generated', and reliability/provenance.py maps all nine agents to 'llm_generated'. EvidenceRecord.confidence is low/medium/high with no source-class axis. Nothing can tell a STANDARD fact from an OMNI_HEURISTIC or AI assertion, so Claude and Codex agreeing cannot be kept separate from validated knowledge.

Architectural consequence (a proposal, not a fact): the core data model should be built around a Fact/Quantity type, roughly {value | UNKNOWN, unit, source_class ∈ {STANDARD, MANUFACTURER, HANDBOOK, OMNI_VALIDATED, OMNI_HEURISTIC, USER_PROVIDED}, source_ref, fact_id}. Typed interfaces, rules, patterns and obligations would all operate on that type. Rule outcomes would use a three-valued logic: any UNKNOWN input yields UNKNOWN unless the rule explicitly declares a justified WARN. Oli would receive a CadObligation set instead of a spec full of defaults. There is a counterweight in the repo: calculation_engine already fails closed (missing_inputs → blocked). Fail-closed behaviour exists locally, but no contract carries it across boundaries.

uncertainties: The defaults in the CAD IR may be deliberate concept-level placeholders (LOD0-LOD2). If Component Intelligence v0.1 feeds Oli through a new IR instead of AssemblySpec, the erasure path in this repository would be avoided, not inherited. Whether the hypothesis is a real integration risk or only a design constraint depends on how Oli will actually consume obligations. That has not been decided and I did not trace it.

I did not trace the end-to-end runtime path from agents/supervisor.py to fusion360_script_generator.py. I have not confirmed that a spec from an LLM agent actually passes through _component()/default_dims() at runtime. No code outside mission_graph was found calling AssemblySpec.from_dict, so the key-dropping path may be dormant.

The fixed penalty for BLOCKED gates (0.15) may already push confidence low enough in practice. I did not measure whether a real report with passing gates plus one BLOCKED gate reads as misleadingly confident.

Value-level epistemic typing adds complexity. A simpler per-finding status, with a coverage check that every required fact was evaluated, might give equivalent fail-closed behaviour for v0.1. This is the main competing design and should be tested, not assumed away.

The ValidationCheck UNKNOWN status may be read outside backend/app/mission_graph (frontend or export). My UNKNOWN grep only covered mission_graph modules and a quoted-literal search across backend/app.

The hypothesis is about how information survives architectural boundaries. It does not decide whether obligations belong on component or interface definitions, or whether a graph or relational representation is better. Those remain open questions for later turns.
requested_action:
Requested of the falsification-biased reviewer (Codex): try to refute this hypothesis.

(1) Find any existing OMNI path where a missing or unknown engineering value reaches CAD output or a report as an explicit unknown rather than a default or a positive score. That would weaken the claim that erasure is systemic.

(2) Argue the competing design: per-finding PASS/WARN/FAIL/UNKNOWN plus a 'required-facts coverage' check, without value-level epistemic typing, gives equivalent fail-closed guarantees for v0.1 with less complexity. Identify a concrete case where the two designs diverge, or show that none exists.

(3) Check whether Oli's CAD handoff actually uses cad_detail_pass_planner and AssemblySpec, which decides whether this is an inherited risk or only a constraint on new design.

A later turn could propose the cheapest distinguishing experiment. For example, a read-only property or fault-injection probe: give the existing planner and IR a component type with unknown dimensions, then check whether any unknown marker survives in to_dict() output. No experiment is proposed or run in this turn.

claim: The primary architectural risk is incomplete assembly semantics: OMNI can omit a required relationship or select an inappropriate assembly configuration while every represented value is KNOWN and preserves its provenance. Value-level epistemic typing cannot detect a requirement that was never instantiated. I propose making a configuration-specific assembly constraint model the core of v0.1, with fact provenance supporting that model. This competes with the claim that value-state preservation is the decisive architectural choice.
mechanism:
The competing mechanism is omission before validation, rather than information erasure during transport. The existing generic planner constructs battery, compute and sensor placeholders even for a shaft mission. Wrapping those dimensions in Known/Unknown types would preserve their epistemic states without establishing the missing shaft, support or retention relationships.

Architectural proposal: represent component instances, typed interface ports, connections, operating cases and selected assembly configurations. Versioned assembly-pattern contracts instantiate required roles and relational constraints from explicit requirements, independently of the connections the candidate happens to contain. Missing applicability information produces UNKNOWN; a missing relationship in an explicitly complete candidate produces FAIL when its governing contract requires that relationship. Unsupported configurations remain UNKNOWN. CAD obligations are derived from the selected configuration and participating interfaces, with links to the requirements, rules and evidence that generated them.

This differs from the already-mentioned required-facts coverage alternative: the obligation set itself depends on topology and configuration, and can be wrong even when all listed facts and checks are complete. As a synthetic example, define a fixture contract requiring exactly one locating support and one floating support. A candidate with two locating supports can contain only known, sourced values and pass every local dimensional check while violating that contract. Neither per-value UNKNOWN propagation nor coverage of the candidate's own fact list discovers the error automatically.

For v0.1, facts can retain units, source references and explicit missing states in a canonical evidence store. An engineering CAD handoff should bind its findings and obligations to an immutable assembly revision and rule-set version. Universal propagation of wrapped values through every legacy CAD field is not yet demonstrated necessary.
evidence: Independently executed a read-only Python -B probe of plan_cad_detail_passes(prompt, {}, 'research_shaft_fixture'). Both 'A supported shaft with bearings and axial retention.' and 'A shaft without bearings or axial retention.' produced LOD2_mechanical_placeholders containing ['battery_pack', 'compute_module', 'sensor_pod']. This demonstrates missing domain interpretation in that fallback, not an observed false engineering PASS.

backend/app/cad/cad_detail_pass_planner.py:451-498 constructs that generic assembly; :517-542 dispatches by platform/family. This is constructive placeholder generation, without a required mechanical relationship model in the inspected path.

The defaulting observation reproduces: _mcomp('test_bearing', 'research_unregistered_bearing').to_dict() returned length_mm=50.0, width_mm=30.0, height_mm=15.0, with empty notes and tags. The helper is named _mcomp, not _component.

The score-collapse claim needs narrowing. backend/app/reliability/gates.py:37-41 preserves BLOCKED as the highest-priority overall status. A read-only probe executing the actual scoring and aggregation function bodies with synthetic gate objects returned confidence=0.76 and overall_status='BLOCKED' for nine PASS gates plus one BLOCKED gate. backend/app/reliability/reliability_service.py:748-787 retains both fields and blockers in the report.

backend/app/reliability/reliability_service.py:615-643 explicitly represents absent rover calculations as missing_evidence and a BLOCKED gate. Thus missing information can survive into a report, although this does not establish complete UNKNOWN semantics.

The export integration is statically reachable: backend/app/export/export_manager.py:1585-1589 calls generate_fusion360_export; backend/app/generators/fusion360_script_generator.py:2600-2617 conditionally calls the detail planner and serializes AssemblySpec. Its arguments are raw mission text, morphology and project type, rather than a Component Intelligence fact payload.

agents/supervisor.py:1006-1012 constructs Oli's fusion360_concept from summary, modeling_plan, component_layout and fabrication_notes. The inspected export planner call does not consume an Oli-supplied typed assembly contract.

The assertion that CAD has no mechanical assembly concepts is too broad: backend/app/cad/cad_assembly_ir.py:52-102 defines mounting features and fastener patterns; :247-257 groups these with components in subassemblies. These provide existing integration shapes, but do not establish typed mating or load-transfer semantics.
uncertainties: The observations establish placeholder generation and preserved BLOCKED reporting; they do not measure which failure mechanism dominates future Component Intelligence workloads.
No full mission, export or Fusion execution was performed. The function probes were in-memory and wrote no files.

A complete implementation of Claude's typed obligations could incorporate configuration-dependent constraint generation. That would combine the hypotheses; their separate contributions would still need testing.

Pattern applicability can itself be incomplete or incorrectly sourced. Deterministic execution does not establish engineering validity, and agreement between agents cannot supply the missing authority.
The locating/floating example is an explicitly stipulated synthetic test contract, not a universal bearing arrangement rule or manufacturer specification.
requested_action: What evidence would distinguish boundary erasure from missing assembly semantics? Propose a controlled 2×2 TestCube experiment: value-state transport on/off crossed with configuration-dependent relational obligation generation on/off. Keep source evidence, local compatibility rules, CAD adapter and acceptance gate fixed. Freeze independently specified fixtures covering missing dimensions, a deleted mandatory connection, and the synthetic locating/floating configuration violation with all values known. Measure preservation of explicit unknowns separately from detection of omitted or contradictory relationships and acceptance of complete valid controls. My prediction is that value typing fixes the missing-value fixture but does not fix relational omissions; configuration constraints detect those without universal value wrappers when canonical evidence lookup remains enforced. Evidence that value typing alone detects those omissions through an independently specified mechanism would weaken my counter-hypothesis. Evidence that combining both factors is necessary would support a joint architecture rather than either claim of primacy.
